reviewers.summary: The quantile regression analysis contains major methodological and reporting issues: the standard error method is unspecified and may be inappropriate, diagnostics are OLS-based and irrelevant, confounder selection is unjustified, and missing data are not addressed. Minor issues include p-value reporting and tau ambiguity. Revision and re-analysis are required.

findings.title: Uncertainty estimation method not specified; potentially misleading standard errors and CI
findings.whyItMatters: Quantile regression requires appropriate standard error estimation (e.g., bootstrap, kernel, or rank inversion). Using OLS-based or misspecified SEs can invalidate inference and confidence intervals.
findings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the standard error method (e.g., rank inversion, bootstrap, etc.). If bootstrap, report bootstrap CIs. Verify that the SE and p-values in stats-run.json correspond to a valid quantile regression SE method.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that stats-run.json 'std_error' values match the output of the declared SE method and are not from an OLS fit.

findings.title: Diagnostics inappropriate for quantile regression; rely on OLS assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: Residual mean, SD, and Shapiro-Wilk test are standard for OLS, not quantile regression. Absence of quantile-specific checks (e.g., residual symmetry, heteroskedasticity by quantile, specification of the conditional quantile function) leaves model adequacy unevaluated.
findings.actionableFix: Replace current diagnostics with quantile-appropriate ones: check residual sign symmetry, plot residuals vs fitted at the chosen quantile, assess heteroskedasticity, and examine influence of observations on the quantile estimate. Remove the Shapiro-Wilk test.
findings.deterministicVerification: Verify that the new diagnostics are appropriate for quantile regression and that OLS-centric outputs are removed.

findings.title: Insufficient adjustment for confounding; no justification for selected covariates
findings.whyItMatters: Observational analyses require transparent confounder selection. Adjusting only for age and severity without a stated rationale or DAG raises strong suspicion of residual confounding, biasing the treatment-outcome association.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a causal diagram or literature-based justification for the included covariates. Consider formal sensitivity analysis (e.g., E-value) for unmeasured confounding, or add further relevant confounders if data permit.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that a confounder selection rationale and, ideally, a sensitivity analysis output are added to the study artifacts.

findings.title: Complete-case analysis with no reporting of missing data extent or mechanism
findings.whyItMatters: If missingness is associated with exposure, outcome, or covariates, complete-case estimates can be biased. Without knowing the amount of missingness or the assumed mechanism, the generalizability and internal validity of the 240 cases are unknown.
findings.actionableFix: Report the total number of eligible observations before exclusion, the proportion of missingness per variable, and the missing data pattern. Discuss whether MCAR, MAR, or MNAR is plausible and, if feasible, conduct a sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation or pattern-mixture models).
findings.deterministicVerification: Verify that a missing data summary and discussion of missingness mechanism have been added to the artifacts.

findings.title: No analysis code or seed provided; run directory contains only output artifacts
findings.whyItMatters: Full reproducibility demands the ability to re-execute the analysis from data to outputs. Without code, the steps (e.g., quantile regression implementation, SE computation) cannot be audited or reproduced by others.
findings.actionableFix: Include the script or notebook that generates the results, along with the random seed. Place it in the run directory and document its use.
findings.deterministicVerification: Run the supplied code and confirm that it reproduces the estimates and diagnostics exactly.

findings.title: P-values reported as 0.0000 in manuscript; lose information and imply impossible exact zero
findings.whyItMatters: Reporting p-values as 0.0000 misleads readers; true p-values are extremely small but not zero (e.g., 3.71e-19 for the intercept). This can distort the perceived strength of evidence.
findings.actionableFix: Report exact p-values (e.g., from stats-run.json) or use p < 0.001 when appropriate. Avoid rounding to four decimal places for tiny values.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that manuscript p-values match stats-run.json with adequate precision.

findings.title: Quantile regression tau (quantile) not explicitly stated; assumption of median unclear
findings.whyItMatters: Quantile regression models a specific conditional quantile, typically the median (tau=0.5). Without stating tau, the interpretation of coefficients is ambiguous, and the claim of 'median association' is unsupported.
findings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the tau (e.g., 0.5 for median) in the Methods and confirm that the software output corresponds to that quantile.
findings.deterministicVerification: Verify that stats-run.json or the new manuscript clearly indicates tau=0.5.

findings.title: No comparison to existing literature or clinical context
findings.whyItMatters: Even a local analysis must be interpreted against prior knowledge. The absence of any literature review prevents assessment of whether the chosen covariates, effect direction, and magnitude are plausible.
findings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review citing relevant studies, and discuss how the current estimates align or differ, noting any clinical or epidemiological context.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript includes a literature section with citations and a discussion of consistency.

missingEvidence: Total sample size before complete-case exclusion and missingness breakdown
Analysis code or script with random seed
Specification of tau (quantile) for quantile regression
Literature references and comparison with prior work

reviewers.summary: The study has major methodological and reporting flaws, including use of inappropriate diagnostics for quantile regression, unaddressed missing data, lack of influence analysis, missing quantile specification, and potential misuse of standard errors. These issues undermine the reliability of the results. The analysis should be revised with proper quantile regression diagnostics, missing data handling, and transparent reporting.

findings.title: Inappropriate diagnostics applied to quantile regression
evidenceRefs: diagnostics.json shows Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals, which is not a valid assumption for quantile regression
findings.whyItMatters: Applying OLS diagnostics to a quantile regression model indicates lack of appropriate model checking, potentially missing heteroscedasticity or specification errors that affect quantile estimates.
findings.actionableFix: Remove Shapiro-Wilk test. Provide quantile-regression-specific diagnostics such as quantile residual plots, specification tests (e.g., resampling-based goodness-of-fit), and heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that shapiro_p_value is not present in the final diagnostics artifact

findings.title: Missing data handling not reported
evidenceRefs: The manuscript and stats-run artifacts show only completeCaseN=240, with no missing data summary or flowchart
findings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis may introduce selection bias if missingness is related to outcome or predictors, and sample size reduction reduces power and generalizability.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a missing data flowchart (number of records excluded, reasons), quantify missingness per variable, and ideally conduct sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation) under MAR assumption.
findings.deterministicVerification: Existence of a missing-data report artifact with counts and patterns

findings.title: Quantile of interest not explicitly stated
evidenceRefs: Manuscript says 'median' but quantile parameter not in stats-run.json; method selection may contain it but not present.
findings.whyItMatters: Reproducibility: The reader cannot verify that the model indeed estimated the median (tau=0.5) without this specification.
findings.actionableFix: Include the quantile (e.g., tau=0.5) in the manuscript Methods and in the stats-run parameters.

findings.title: P-values reported as 0.0000
evidenceRefs: Manuscript shows p=0.0000 for several terms, while actual values are <1e-19
findings.whyItMatters: Misleading precision; many journals require p < 0.001 or exact values in scientific notation. Can obscure extreme significance but not a major flaw.
findings.actionableFix: Report p-values as p < 0.001 or use scientific notation (e.g., p=3.71e-19).
findings.deterministicVerification: Manuscript text contains p<0.001 or scientific notation

findings.title: Lack of influence diagnostics
evidenceRefs: Manuscript acknowledges 'No explicit influence diagnostic evidence was found.' Affirmed by missing influence artifacts.
findings.whyItMatters: With only 240 observations and an observational design, a few influential points could drive the results. Without influence analysis, robustness is unproven.
findings.actionableFix: Perform influence diagnostics appropriate for quantile regression (e.g., DFBETAS for quantile regression, leave-one-out changes) and report any influential cases.
findings.deterministicVerification: Presence of an influence diagnostic file or table

findings.title: No assessment of functional form or interactions
evidenceRefs: Manuscript only includes linear terms for age and severity; no mention of nonlinearity or interaction checks
findings.whyItMatters: Quantile regression estimates can be biased if relationships are nonlinear or there are omitted interactions, especially for small datasets. Model misspecification could invalidate the reported effects.
findings.actionableFix: Consider including squared terms, splines, or testing for interactions. Provide evidence of linearity assumption (e.g., component-plus-residual plots adapted for quantile regression).
findings.deterministicVerification: Model diagnostics showing functional form checks

findings.title: No software, version, or code provided
evidenceRefs: Artifacts contain no session info, script, or package versions.
findings.whyItMatters: Reproducibility requires knowing the computational environment and exact code used to produce the estimates.
findings.actionableFix: Include a sessionInfo() output or software citation, and provide the analysis script in the supplementary materials.

findings.title: Standard error computation method unclear, potentially invalid
evidenceRefs: stats-run.json provides std_error and CI but no indication of method (e.g., bootstrap, asymptotic, kernel). Diagnostics show 'weighted: false', which suggests no robust SE correction.
findings.whyItMatters: Quantile regression standard errors require special handling due to heteroscedasticity. Using default linear regression SE can produce invalid CIs and p-values.
findings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the standard error computation method (e.g., bootstrap with R repeats, or asymptotic with sparsity estimation via Hall-Sheather). Verify with simulation or bootstrap. Report the method in the manuscript.
findings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json includes 'se_method' field, and diagnostics confirm appropriateness

missingEvidence: Missing data report (counts, proportions, patterns, reasons)
Software session info and analysis code

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
